record_type_quote:
This study examined whether outcomes in early intensive behavioral
intervention (EIBI) during a university-led multisite project could be replicated
by the same community agency independently of the project.

targets.authors: Cohen, H., Amerine-Dickens, M. S., & Smith, T.
targets.title: Early intensive behavioral treatment: Replication of the UCLA model in a community setting.
targets.evidence_quote:
The current report extends the
literature on EIBI outcome in two ways: First, it examines whether outcomes
in a university-led multisite project (Cohen et al., 2006) could be replicated
with children seen by the same community agency outside of the project.
targets.outcome_quote:
Overall, gains appear comparable to those in our prior study

 20

Behavior Modification 44(1)

(Cohen et al., 2006) and in other reports on EIBI (Eldevik et al., 2009).
Because these children were seen independently of the university-led project
that was involved in our previous study, the results indicate that favorable
outcomes can be sustained in a community setting.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The report explicitly re-tests the same agency’s university-led project outcomes in different children outside that project. The authors judge gains comparable to Cohen et al. (2006) and conclude that favorable community outcomes were sustained.

targets.authors: Eikeseth, S., Smith, T., Jahr, E., & Eldevik, S.
targets.title: Outcome for children with autism who began intensive behavioral treatment between ages 4 and 7.
targets.evidence_quote:
The present study supports previous findings from investigators such as
Eikeseth et al. (2007) that EIBI, using the Lovaas/UCLA Model, can be
implemented in a nonuniversity setting and that favorable results can be
achieved for children above the age of 3½ years at entry into treatment.
targets.outcome_quote:
In addition, given the
wide age range of our sample, the results also support previous findings that
some children who are 4 to 6 years old at onset of EIBI can make substantial
gains in IQ, adaptive behavior, and school placement (Eikeseth et al., 2007).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The report also re-tests efficacy when intervention begins after early preschool age. It explicitly identifies its results as supporting Eikeseth et al. (2007) for substantial gains among children starting at ages 4–6. The 2007 outcome report is the closest cited target for this longer-term finding; the 2002 interim report is not separately targeted.

reasoning: Completed new-sample replication with 48 EIBI children and 46 matched services-as-usual children. Two specific published findings are tested: maintenance of the Cohen et al. (2006) community-agency outcomes outside the university-led project and the Eikeseth et al. (2007) finding of benefit for children entering at older ages. Lovaas and other intervention, age-predictor, review, and measurement references supply background or methods rather than additional independently targeted findings. This coding concerns only the supplied intact report.
